text.p: Indonesian pharmaceutical firm PT Kalbe Farma said on Wednesday that a restructuring programme to re-focus on its core business was on track.
Kalbe Farma president director Budi Dharma said the proceeds of its divestment from some non-pharmaceutical businesses would be used for enhancing performance in the firm's core activities.
"We are re-focusing on pharmaceutical products. Therefore, we are re-emphasing our marketing in that area," Dharma said in an interview.
Last year, Kalbe completed the sale of its confectionery unit PT Helios Arya Putera and is in the midst of divesting its majority stake in plastics manufacturer PT Igar Jaya
It is also awaiting shareholder approval to sell off its packaging division.

Dharma said the proceeds would be used first to repay loans and then to expand pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities or acquire other companies. He said the firm was also committed to enlarging its marketing network and paying dividends, but he declined to give estimated figures or details of the moves.
Dharma also said the company had brought forward by one year a revamped marketing strategy.
"To strenghten our presence in the market, we might re-launch old products which have not been successful, seek new licences, or acquisitions," he said.
He said the company has decided to expand its operations overseas with the focus on neighbouring countries such as the Philippines, Burma and Vietnam.
"We are planning to become a regional player. So we are always looking for a possibility to expand into this region," he said without elaborating.
He said the company expected to maintain profit growth at about an annual 15-20 percent in 1997 and the next few years.
On Tuesday, shares of Kalbe Farma rose about 6.3 percent in active trading on a newspaper report that it would announce positive first quarter results, brokers said.

The Indonesian Observer said on Tuesday that the company was likely to post a net profit of 21 billion rupiah ($8.63 million) in the first quarter of 1997 and a full year net profit of 83.4 billion rupiah. Dharma refused to comment on the report.
The company booked net income of 73.11 billion rupiah in 1996 against 65.27 billion rupiah in 1995.
Brokerage firm Asia Equity has forecast that Kalbe Farma will post net profit of 81.6 billion rupiah and 94.9 billion rupiah in 1997 and 1998 respectively.
On Wednesday, Kalbe shares were down 50 rupiah at 2,775 in late trade. ($1 = 2,433 rupiah)
